title.narrative: Supporting documentary heritage preservation in GCC and Yemen

description.narrative: Documentary heritage is a vital source of collective memory, cultural identity, and knowledge transmission. In Yemen, years of conflict have continued to place documentary heritage collections at risk due to physical deterioration, limited preservation capacities, insufficient documentation systems, and the absence of comprehensive emergency preparedness mechanisms. At the same time, GCC countries are increasingly investing in the preservation, digitization, and accessibility of documentary heritage, creating opportunities for regional cooperation and knowledge exchange. Building on the documentary heritage mapping and needs assessment conducted in the Arab region and in KSA, as well as the strategic partnership established with Qatar National Library and the creation of the new established MOWCAR, UNESCO will continue supporting the preservation, safeguarding, and promotion of documentary heritage in Yemen while fostering regional collaboration among memory institutions across the GCC. Activities will include strengthening capacities in collection management, inventorying, digitization, preventive conservation, disaster risk management, and emergency preparedness; supporting the identification and nomination of documentary heritage collections to the UNESCO Memory of the World Programme; promoting digital access to documentary heritage; and facilitating regional knowledge-sharing among libraries, archives, museums, and other memory institutions. The programme will also support the development of practical tools, guidelines, and institutional partnerships aimed at enhancing the long-term resilience, accessibility, and visibility of documentary heritage collections. Particular attention will be given to protecting documentary heritage at risk, advancing digital preservation practices, and mobilizing partnerships and resources for larger-scale preservation initiatives in Yemen and the Gulf region.
